title: Shemirat Halashon 32
summary: Rabbi Soffer discusses topics in Shemirat Halashon regarding rechilut, including how Hashem left out details when repeating Sarah's words to Abraham to maintain peace. He covers speaking rechilut through hinting, instigating past disagreements, and whether statements made in front of three people may be repeated. He also explains scenarios involving business partners or match prospects looking elsewhere and the potential emotional distress caused by revealing such information.
questions: Why did Hashem leave out Sarah's comment about Abraham being old when speaking to Abraham?
Is it considered rechilut to hint at negative information without stating a person's name directly?
How does the rule of three people apply to repeating gossip?
Is a person permitted to tell their business partner that they secretly looked for another partner?
